chapters.title: Chapter 1: There Is No Good Answer

episode.tagline: How does one plan for retirement? What amount of money does one need to be sorted? Can you even arrive at a number?
episode.about: In this episode, Ajay explains why the question itself is misguided — and the approach one should take towards our future in such an uncertain world.

items.content: Amit's intro hype for Ajay's personal finance module: 'People could have written songs about it, made films on it, written poetry on it,…
Amit introduces Ajay as a picture of calm, 'absolute shanti', yet asking him the retirement question three times produced 'violence'.…
Ajay on longevity, pointing to the 21-year-old crew member Nomsita: she has to realistically plan to be 'an active little old lady doing…
Ajay catches himself mid-argument about rising wages: 'the price you will pay for a cook, for a driver, oops, driverless cars. Scratch…
Ajay on how easy investing has become: 'It is like 3x harder to use Zerodha than it is to use Zepto.'
When Ajay suggests redirecting restaurant and alcohol spending into savings, Amit protests: 'Alcohol, though I don't have, but Swiggy is…
Amit's offer to Chinese viewers trapped by capital controls: 'You send an apartment my way or a full house, the country villa, perhaps,…
Amit's grammar grievance: 'societal' is just a fancy academic word for 'social', so 'it broke my heart, Ajay Shah, to see you fall under…
Amit's answer to an untrustworthy state is a mock crypto pitch: 'We are introducing a new cryptocurrency. We can call it everything…
A callback to Ajay's line that CDs will become 'museum pieces': Amit recommends Led Zeppelin, noting the CD beside Ajay is 'worthless,…
Baumol's cost disease: economist William Baumol's insight that labour-intensive services keep rising in price relative to goods. Ajay…
Hitler, 1933: Ajay says capital controls originated with Hitler and had disappeared from all rich countries by the late seventies.
Magna Carta: Ajay calls the freedom to use your money as you like 'a magna carta right.'
Japan's bathing robots: Ajay notes that Japan is building robots to bathe frail elderly people, a personal service being automated.
20 February 2015: the date India's inflation targeting framework began. Ajay says the state now has to prove its mettle over the next…
